## Introduction

The rise of the AfD has sparked interest in understanding the factors that influence the support for right-wing/extreme parties. Economic reasons are often cited as key factors. This project tries to visualize the linkage between these two. 

## Research Question

To what extent do economic fluctuations (measured by GDP, growth, or a decline in GDP) influence voting intention and the polling numbers of the AfD?

## Data

We use the ALLBUS Cumulative Data Set together with official economic statistics from German federal statistical agencies. The ALLBUS dataset was chosen because it provides reliable and nationally representative survey data for Germany, covering a wide range of socio-demographic characteristics, political attitudes, and opinions on social issues. To complement these survey data, we incorporate official statistics on GDP and unemployment.

## Results

AfD support remained relatively stable until 2022 before increasing sharply. Descriptive analyses suggest that weaker economic conditions, particularly in the post-pandemic period, were associated with higher AfD support. However, these findings are exploratory and require confirmation through regression analysis.
